title: Highway Safe Following Distance Rule
text: In highway driving scenarios, the vehicle should maintain a safe following distance sufficient to avoid rear-end collisions. When relative speed is high and longitudinal spacing is small, the vehicle should prioritize deceleration and avoid further compressing the following distance. Trigger condition: ttc_lt=3.0, thw_lt=1.2. Risk mechanism: Insufficient time headway or short TTC reduces reaction time and increases rear-end collision risk. Relevant metrics: TTC, THW, headway, distance, relative_speed.
risk_mechanism: Insufficient time headway or short TTC reduces reaction time and increases rear-end collision risk.

title: Prohibition of Continuously Compressing Following Distance
text: During car-following, the vehicle should not continuously accelerate to reduce the distance to the lead vehicle. When relative speed is positive and spacing is continuously decreasing, the vehicle should prioritize reducing speed to restore a safe gap. Trigger condition: closing_speed_gt=0.0, distance_decreasing, ttc_lt=4.0, thw_lt=1.5. Risk mechanism: Insufficient time headway or short TTC reduces reaction time and increases rear-end collision risk. Relevant metrics: TTC, THW, headway, distance, relative_speed.
risk_mechanism: Insufficient time headway or short TTC reduces reaction time and increases rear-end collision risk.

title: Highway Lane-Change Gap Acceptance Rule
text: Before changing lanes at highway speed, the vehicle should confirm that sufficient safe gaps exist both ahead of and behind it in the target lane. If the rear vehicle is approaching quickly or the available gap is insufficient, the vehicle should not perform a forced cut-in. Trigger condition: target_lane_gap_lt=15.0, rear_vehicle_closing_speed_gt=2.0, ttc_lt=4.0. Risk mechanism: A small target-lane gap or rapidly decreasing TTC can compress the rear vehicle reaction space during lane change. Relevant metrics: TTC, headway, relative_speed.
risk_mechanism: A small target-lane gap or rapidly decreasing TTC can compress the rear vehicle reaction space during lane change.

title: Prohibition of Forced Merging
text: A lane-changing vehicle must not force its way into a lane by compressing the safety space of the rear vehicle. Such behavior significantly increases the risk of emergency braking or collision for the rear vehicle. Trigger condition: target_lane_gap_lt=15.0, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.5. Risk mechanism: A small target-lane gap or rapidly decreasing TTC can compress the rear vehicle reaction space during lane change. Relevant metrics: TTC, DCPA, min_future_distance, distance, headway.
risk_mechanism: A small target-lane gap or rapidly decreasing TTC can compress the rear vehicle reaction space during lane change.

title: Avoid Forced Cut-in on Highways
text: In highway scenarios, the vehicle should not rely on forced cut-in behavior to obtain passage. If the lane change would significantly compress the rear vehicle's reaction space or cause the minimum TTC to drop rapidly, the maneuver should be aborted immediately. Trigger condition: target_lane_gap_lt=15.0, ttc_lt=3.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.0. Risk mechanism: A small target-lane gap or rapidly decreasing TTC can compress the rear vehicle reaction space during lane change. Relevant metrics: TTC, min_future_distance, distance, headway.
risk_mechanism: A small target-lane gap or rapidly decreasing TTC can compress the rear vehicle reaction space during lane change.

title: Roundabout Entry Yield Rule for Circulating Vehicles
text: When entering a roundabout, the vehicle should yield first to vehicles already circulating inside the roundabout, and must not force its way in by accelerating, rushing ahead, or compressing the available gap. Trigger condition: in_roundabout_vehicle_present, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.5. Risk mechanism: Roundabout entry conflicts are dominated by closest approach distance and future spatial proximity to circulating vehicles. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance, headway.
risk_mechanism: Roundabout entry conflicts are dominated by closest approach distance and future spatial proximity to circulating vehicles.

title: Priority Principle for Vehicles Inside a Roundabout
text: When driving inside a roundabout, the vehicle should follow the existing order of movement and avoid sudden lane changes or acceleration through gaps, in order to maintain overall traffic-flow stability. Trigger condition: in_roundabout, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.5. Risk mechanism: Sudden speed or lane-order changes inside a roundabout can disturb priority order and create short-distance conflicts. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance, headway.
risk_mechanism: Sudden speed or lane-order changes inside a roundabout can disturb priority order and create short-distance conflicts.

title: Cyclist Priority Protection at Roundabout Exits
text: When exiting a roundabout, if cyclists are present near the exit, the vehicle should reduce speed and preserve sufficient safety distance, and must not cut out ahead of the cyclist. Trigger condition: vrus_present, roundabout_exit, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.0. Risk mechanism: A cyclist near the roundabout exit has low physical protection, and low future distance can create a crossing or close-pass conflict. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance.
risk_mechanism: A cyclist near the roundabout exit has low physical protection, and low future distance can create a crossing or close-pass conflict.

title: Maintain Safe Spacing During Close Parallel Movement in Roundabouts
text: When parallel movement or merging interactions occur inside a roundabout, the vehicle should reduce speed and maintain sufficient lateral and longitudinal spacing to avoid dangerous interactions. Trigger condition: dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.5. Risk mechanism: Parallel or converging movement with low lateral/longitudinal clearance increases the probability of side-swipe or merging conflict. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance, lateral_clearance.
risk_mechanism: Parallel or converging movement with low lateral/longitudinal clearance increases the probability of side-swipe or merging conflict.

title: Priority Protection Principle for Vulnerable Road Users
text: In scenarios involving vulnerable road users such as cyclists or pedestrians, motor vehicles should actively reduce speed and increase safety margins, prioritizing the safety of vulnerable road users. Trigger condition: vrus_present, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.0. Risk mechanism: Low clearance to a cyclist leaves limited room for sudden deviation and increases vulnerable-road-user collision severity. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance.
risk_mechanism: Low clearance to a cyclist leaves limited room for sudden deviation and increases vulnerable-road-user collision severity.

title: Safety Takes Priority Over Traffic Efficiency
text: In traffic decision-making, when safety conflicts with efficiency, safety should be prioritized. The vehicle should avoid improving travel efficiency by compressing spacing or forcing passage. Trigger condition: safety_efficiency_conflict. Risk mechanism: Choosing efficiency over safety can shrink margins and amplify collision risk under uncertainty. Relevant metrics: TTC, DCPA, min_future_distance.
risk_mechanism: Choosing efficiency over safety can shrink margins and amplify collision risk under uncertainty.

title: Roundabout Exit Passing and Yielding Rule
text: When exiting a roundabout, the vehicle should consider the positions and speeds of nearby vehicles and other traffic participants near the exit, and should not cut out ahead when safety distance is insufficient. Trigger condition: roundabout_exit, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.5. Risk mechanism: At a roundabout exit, limited spacing or visibility can create short-horizon conflicts with nearby traffic participants. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance, visibility.
risk_mechanism: At a roundabout exit, limited spacing or visibility can create short-horizon conflicts with nearby traffic participants.

title: Cyclist Priority Protection Rule in Roundabouts
text: When interacting with cyclists in a roundabout, motor vehicles should adopt a more conservative strategy, maintain sufficient longitudinal and lateral safety distance, and avoid compressing the cyclist's space through priority forcing or close passing. Trigger condition: vrus_present, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.0. Risk mechanism: Low clearance to a cyclist leaves limited room for sudden deviation and increases vulnerable-road-user collision severity. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance, lateral_clearance.
risk_mechanism: Low clearance to a cyclist leaves limited room for sudden deviation and increases vulnerable-road-user collision severity.

title: Prohibition of Forced Priority in Roundabouts
text: In roundabout interactions, the vehicle should not obtain priority by forcing its way through or compressing others' space. It should maintain safe order through deceleration or waiting. Trigger condition: dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.5. Risk mechanism: Forcing priority in a roundabout compresses another participant's safety margin and can trigger emergency braking or collision. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance.
risk_mechanism: Forcing priority in a roundabout compresses another participant's safety margin and can trigger emergency braking or collision.

title: Visibility and Deceleration Requirement at Roundabout Exits
text: When exiting a roundabout, the vehicle should account for risks caused by limited exit visibility, reduce speed in advance, and preserve reaction space. Trigger condition: roundabout_exit, limited_visibility, min_future_distance_lt=3.0. Risk mechanism: At a roundabout exit, limited spacing or visibility can create short-horizon conflicts with nearby traffic participants. Relevant metrics: min_future_distance, distance, visibility.
risk_mechanism: At a roundabout exit, limited spacing or visibility can create short-horizon conflicts with nearby traffic participants.

title: Urban Pedestrian Priority Protection Rule
text: When a pedestrian approaches or may enter the vehicle's predicted path, the vehicle should yield proactively and reduce speed. It must not compress the pedestrian's passage space by accelerating or forcing a detour around the pedestrian. Trigger condition: vrus_present, ttc_lt=3.0, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.0. Risk mechanism: A pedestrian close to the predicted vehicle path creates a short-horizon crossing conflict with limited reaction time. Relevant metrics: TTC, DCPA, min_future_distance, distance.
risk_mechanism: A pedestrian close to the predicted vehicle path creates a short-horizon crossing conflict with limited reaction time.

title: Crosswalk Pedestrian Yield Rule
text: When approaching a crosswalk, the vehicle should observe in advance and reduce speed. When pedestrians are on or near the crosswalk, the vehicle should yield and be prepared to stop. Trigger condition: vrus_present, near_crosswalk, min_future_distance_lt=3.0. Risk mechanism: Pedestrians near a crosswalk may enter the vehicle path with limited warning, requiring conservative yielding behavior. Relevant metrics: min_future_distance, distance.
risk_mechanism: Pedestrians near a crosswalk may enter the vehicle path with limited warning, requiring conservative yielding behavior.

title: Cautious Passing and Yielding Rule at Urban Intersections
text: When passing through an urban intersection, the vehicle should reduce speed and continuously monitor conflict points. When traffic participants from crossing directions are nearby or their trajectories intersect, the vehicle should yield or stop and wait. Trigger condition: near_intersection, dcpa_lt=2.5, min_future_distance_lt=3.0. Risk mechanism: Intersection conflicts involve crossing trajectories where small future distance can rapidly become a collision conflict. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance.
risk_mechanism: Intersection conflicts involve crossing trajectories where small future distance can rapidly become a collision conflict.

title: Urban Cyclist Yielding and Protection Rule
text: When interacting with cyclists on urban roads, motor vehicles should maintain sufficient lateral and longitudinal safety distance, decelerate and yield when necessary, and avoid close-range priority forcing or close passing. Trigger condition: vrus_present, dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.5. Risk mechanism: Cyclists have unstable trajectories and limited physical protection, so low clearance creates high injury risk. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance, lateral_clearance.
risk_mechanism: Cyclists have unstable trajectories and limited physical protection, so low clearance creates high injury risk.

title: Cyclist Lateral Safety Clearance Rule
text: When a vehicle passes or approaches a cyclist, it should maintain sufficient lateral safety clearance. If lateral clearance is insufficient, the vehicle should slow down and wait for a safe passing opportunity. Trigger condition: vrus_present, dcpa_lt=1.5, min_future_distance_lt=2.0. Risk mechanism: Low lateral clearance to a cyclist leaves insufficient space for unexpected cyclist deviation or vehicle control errors. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, distance, lateral_clearance.
risk_mechanism: Low lateral clearance to a cyclist leaves insufficient space for unexpected cyclist deviation or vehicle control errors.

title: Low-TTC Collision Avoidance Rule
text: When time to collision is short or the predicted minimum future distance is small, the vehicle should reduce speed, increase the safety margin, and avoid actions that further compress reaction time. Trigger condition: ttc_lt=3.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.5. Risk mechanism: Low TTC indicates that available reaction time is limited and evasive action must be taken early. Relevant metrics: TTC, min_future_distance, distance.
risk_mechanism: Low TTC indicates that available reaction time is limited and evasive action must be taken early.

title: Deceleration Rule Under Limited Visibility
text: When visibility is limited or potential conflict points are difficult to observe in time, the vehicle should reduce speed in advance and increase safety distance, avoiding high-speed passage or aggressive lane changes. Trigger condition: limited_visibility, min_future_distance_lt=3.0. Risk mechanism: Limited visibility reduces perception range and increases the probability of late conflict detection. Relevant metrics: min_future_distance, distance, visibility.
risk_mechanism: Limited visibility reduces perception range and increases the probability of late conflict detection.

title: Target-Lane Safety Check Rule Before Lane Change
text: Before changing lanes at highway speed, the vehicle should confirm that vehicles ahead of and behind it in the target lane both have sufficient safety gaps. If the rear vehicle is approaching rapidly or the gap is insufficient, the vehicle should abandon the lane change and wait for a safer opportunity. Trigger condition: target_lane_gap_lt=15.0, rear_vehicle_closing_speed_gt=2.0, ttc_lt=4.0. Risk mechanism: Insufficient target-lane gap and high rear-vehicle closing speed can force the rear vehicle into emergency braking. Relevant metrics: TTC, headway, relative_speed.
risk_mechanism: Insufficient target-lane gap and high rear-vehicle closing speed can force the rear vehicle into emergency braking.

title: Pedestrian Yield Rule at Roundabout Exits
text: When exiting a roundabout, if pedestrians are present near the exit or may enter the vehicle path, the vehicle should decelerate in advance and yield. It must not cut out ahead of them. Trigger condition: vrus_present, near_roundabout_exit, min_future_distance_lt=3.0. Risk mechanism: Pedestrians near a roundabout exit may conflict with exiting vehicles whose paths curve and visibility may be limited. Relevant metrics: min_future_distance, distance, visibility.
risk_mechanism: Pedestrians near a roundabout exit may conflict with exiting vehicles whose paths curve and visibility may be limited.

title: Vulnerable Road User Protection Rule at Roundabout Entries
text: Before entering a roundabout, if pedestrians or cyclists are present near the entry, the vehicle should reduce speed and yield proactively. It must not compress the vulnerable road users' space by accelerating into the roundabout. Trigger condition: vrus_present, near_roundabout_entry, dcpa_lt=2.0. Risk mechanism: VRUs near a roundabout entry can be occluded by traffic geometry and may cross the entry path unexpectedly. Relevant metrics: DCPA.
risk_mechanism: VRUs near a roundabout entry can be occluded by traffic geometry and may cross the entry path unexpectedly.

title: Conservative Control Rule Under Emergency Braking Risk
text: When required deceleration is high and time to collision is short, the vehicle should immediately adopt conservative control, reduce speed, and avoid creating new merging, priority-forcing, or close-following conflicts. Trigger condition: drac_gt=6.0, ttc_lt=3.0. Risk mechanism: High required deceleration indicates that maintaining the current motion may soon require emergency braking to avoid collision. Relevant metrics: TTC, DRAC.
risk_mechanism: High required deceleration indicates that maintaining the current motion may soon require emergency braking to avoid collision.

title: Safety Margin Recovery Rule
text: When the predicted closest approach distance or minimum future distance is too small, the vehicle should prioritize recovering spatial safety margins, including deceleration, increasing longitudinal headway, or increasing lateral clearance. Trigger condition: dcpa_lt=2.0, min_future_distance_lt=2.0. Risk mechanism: Small closest approach distance and low predicted future distance indicate insufficient spatial safety margin. Relevant metrics: DCPA, min_future_distance, headway, distance, lateral_clearance.
risk_mechanism: Small closest approach distance and low predicted future distance indicate insufficient spatial safety margin.
